claims.text: Toughness retention is governed by the stability of a fine, dual-phase dendritic microstructure.
Coherent elemental partitioning between BCC regions contributes to toughness retention.
Moderate thermal annealing produces microstructural coarsening.
Microstructural coarsening leads to brittle intermetallic precipitation at phase boundaries.
Boundary precipitation of brittle intermetallic phases reduces resistance to crack propagation and overall toughness.
The initial as-cast alloy has a fine, dual-phase dendritic microstructure containing coherent BCC phases and controlled elemental segregation.
Annealing 50–100 °C above the intended service temperature for a prolonged period can initiate brittle intermetallic precipitation without causing complete transformation.
Retention of toughness depends on maintaining a stable, finely dispersed phase structure.
Coarsening and intermetallic precipitation mediate toughness loss.
The fine dual-phase microstructure and controlled elemental partitioning facilitate localized plastic deformation.
The fine dual-phase microstructure and controlled elemental partitioning impede crack propagation through strong grain-boundary cohesion and effective work hardening.
Thermal annealing accelerates diffusion and causes coarser phase segregation.
Brittle intermetallic phases formed along phase boundaries act as crack-nucleation sites.
Boundary intermetallic phases accelerate crack propagation and lower toughness.
Annealed samples will have lower plastic strain than the as-cast baseline.
Annealed samples will exhibit more microcracking and scratch-induced damage than the as-cast baseline.
Annealed samples will have lower fracture toughness than the as-cast baseline.
The reduction in toughness will correlate with microstructural coarsening and the emergence of brittle secondary phases.
The as-cast baseline exhibits high toughness and ductility at room temperature and moderately elevated temperatures.
The proposed behavior applies below temperatures or exposure durations that trigger a full phase transformation.
